# Introduction

Every model in `diseasy` contains some parameterisation of its forecasts.
These parameters can then be optimised to align model forecasts with the
real-world observations.

This operation requires only two components:
1) A metric for the optimiser to optimise
2) Free parameters for the optimiser to control

# Model parameterisation
Models `diseasy` will contain parameters that are either specific to the model
(e.g. the compartment structure in `?DiseasyModelOdeSeir`) or parameters meant
to control the functional modules passed to the model (e.g. `?DiseasySeason`).

For example, lets consider the parameters of `?DiseasyModelG0`:
```{r DiseasyModelG0 - parameters}
model <- DiseasyModelG0$new()
model$parameters
```

This model has parameters inherent to the model and parameters related to the
season module. This latter type of parameters, parameters that should modify
the internal modules are treated specially:
If these parameters are `NULL` they will inherit the defaults (if any) from the
module. If they are different from `NULL` they will be applied to the module.

A couple of examples:
```{r DiseasyModelG0 - controlling season}
# We create a default season module which includes a "no seasonality" scenario
# with no parameters
season <- DiseasySeason$new(reference_date = Sys.Date())

model_1 <- DiseasyModelG0$new(season = season)
print(model_1$parameters)


# If we change to the "covid_season_v1" season model, we have a single "scale"
# parameter in the season model
season$use_covid_season_v1()

model_2 <- DiseasyModelG0$new(season = season)
print(model_2$parameters) # ... and this scale is copied to the model


# If we change to the "cosine_Season" season model, we have both a "scale"
# parameter and a "peak" parameter in the season model
season$use_cosine_season()

model_3 <- DiseasyModelG0$new(season = season)
print(model_3$parameters) # ... and these are copied to the model


# If we provide specific values to the model, then these values are
# passed to the season module.
model_4 <- DiseasyModelG0$new(
  season = season,
  parameters = list("season.scale" = 0.5)
)
print(model_4$parameters) # "peak" value is still copied
print(attr(model_4$season$model_t, "dots"))
```
